instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Mental health tech company offering an app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program with human therapist chat support. 18,000 active users. Clinical evidence from a published RCT showing 40% reduction in PHQ-9 scores. Expanding into corporate wellness programs and evaluating AI-supported therapist productivity tools.
answers.pastInitiatives: Our engineering team adopted an agile methodology last year, moving from waterfall-style quarterly releases to 2-week sprints with continuous deployment. This reduced our release cycle time by 60% and improved cross-functional collaboration. However, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are still adapting to the faster cadence.
answers.strategicGoals: We are targeting a 20% improvement in operational throughput without increasing headcount. Our processes have grown organically over the years and are overdue for standardization. We suspect that workflow digitization, basic automation, and better data integration between our core systems can unlock significant productivity gains within our current cost structure.
answers.additionalContext: Our industry is facing a pending regulatory shift that will require mandatory carbon emissions reporting and supply chain due diligence starting next fiscal year. Innovation efforts must account for compliance infrastructure investment as a non-negotiable prerequisite to growth initiatives.
answers.teamSize: Our digital and innovation organization includes 80+ professionals across centers of excellence for AI/ML, cloud engineering, UX design, and agile delivery. We run an internal incubator program that has graduated 6 new digital products to market in the past 2 years, alongside a corporate venture capital arm that makes strategic minority investments in relevant startups.

opportunities.title: AI-Driven Intake and Triage Automation
opportunities.rationale: Implementing machine learning models to automate initial patient assessment and appropriate therapist matching can significantly reduce manual scheduling time and improve first-contact efficiency. This is a low-risk, high-impact incremental gain that directly addresses the efficiency priority.

first_actions: Define MVP scope for intake automation using existing user data pipelines.
Run a 3-month pilot program with one business unit.
execution_plan.success_metric: 25% reduction in average time from patient sign-up to therapist assignment.
milestones: Q3: Model training completion and sandbox testing.
Q4: Pilot launch and KPI review.

opportunities.title: B2B Corporate Wellness Platform Integration (Subscription Model)
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging the core therapeutic IP to create a scalable B2B corporate wellness offering targets high-volume, predictable revenue streams and leverages existing clinical success. While requiring significant cultural shift, this moves beyond simple app features into creating a new market segment that offers higher margins.

first_actions: Conduct feasibility study on B2B product licensing structure.
Establish a dedicated cross-functional task force (Legal, Sales, Product).
execution_plan.success_metric: Secure 3 pilot B2B corporate contracts generating $1M ARR within 18 months.
milestones: Q1: Market validation and pricing model lock.
Q4: Launch MVP of the B2B platform.

next_steps.action: Conduct a comprehensive process mapping exercise across core business units to identify the top 5 non-value-added workflow bottlenecks.
Allocate $20k immediately for the AI-driven intake pilot project and assign a dedicated technical lead to initiate sprint planning.
Establish a formal 'Innovation Governance' subcommittee within the executive steering committee to streamline ROI approval for all efficiency initiatives.

key_weaknesses: High dependency on centralized decision-making, leading to slow response times in business unit innovation.
Inconsistent adoption of new agile methodologies across adjacent non-engineering teams (marketing, support).
Lack of standardized data collection infrastructure required for emerging regulatory compliance demands.
Risk aversion inherent in the conservative appetite may stifle necessary radical digital transformation.
